quote: “Let no one be slow to seek wisdom when he is young nor weary in the search thereof when he is grown old.”
source: Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus, in Diogenes Laertius, Lives X.122 (trans. R. D. Hicks, 1925)

evidence.where: Hicks translation of the letter reproduced with translator credit at EpicureanFriends (Hicks, Bailey and Yonge versions side by side); Wikisource Book X identifies the text as Hicks; Perseus was down
evidence.edition: R. D. Hicks, Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, Loeb Classical Library vol. II, 1925
evidence.locator: Book X, section 122, first sentence of the Letter to Menoeceus

reason: The opening sentence of the letter in Hicks matches the proposal word for word, confirmed in a secondary reproduction that credits Hicks 1925 explicitly; the Loeb page itself is paywalled. Not shipped, not at cap, not banned.
